statements.t: Following management’s formal remarks, there will be a question-and-answer session.

“We believe that our CardiAMP autologous cell therapy is on track to be the first approved minimally invasive biologic therapy for the treatment of heart failure in a first world country based on the recent interactions with Japan’s Pharmaceutical and Medical Devices Agency,” said Peter Altman, PhD, Chief Executive Officer of BioCardia.

“In addition, in the coming months, we aim to be able to submit our Helix transendocardial delivery platform for FDA approval, which would be the first delivery system of its type approved in the United States.
Slower than targeted enrollment could delay completion of our clinical trials and delay or prevent the development of our therapeutic candidates.

risks.t: the inherent uncertainties associated with developing new products or technologies
the ability to raise the additional funding needed to continue to pursue BioCardia’s business and product development plans
the ability to enter licensing and partnering arrangements and overall market conditions
